author: gpt-5.6-luna
keyExtra: Locations are source file paths, each key item a different file.
brief:
Phase: testing and QA. Role: QA engineer. Repo kind: a Node.js data synchronisation service that copies customer records from a legacy store to a new one: a batch migrator with checkpoints and resume, a change-capture reader, a field mapper with type conversions, a conflict resolver (last write wins with a tie rule), a dead-letter queue, a verification job, an admin CLI, a generated mapping table (large, low risk), docs, CI config, a small existing suite. The task is NOT to write tests; it is to plan them: the agent writes docs/TEST-STRATEGY.md saying where the real risk is, the severity and the test for each, with a JSON list at the end. Seed 8 real risk areas found only by reading code (for example: a checkpoint written before the batch commit so a crash skips records, a mapper that truncates or coerces a value silently, a tie rule that depends on iteration order, a retry that re-applies a non-idempotent change, a verification job that compares counts only, a timezone-naive timestamp comparison, a dead-letter queue that drops the failure reason, a resume path that is never exercised). Add decoys: the large generated mapping table and a messy legacy export script are low risk.

The request is from a QA lead who has two weeks before a migration weekend: 'what do we test, in what order, and what happens if we skip the rest'.

items.text: Plans a full rehearsal or shadow run on production-shaped data with realistic volume, skew and dirty records, and uses it to time the weekend window.
items.source: Stripe, Online migrations at scale, https://stripe.com/blog/online-migrations (vendor copyright; idea only)

items.text: Defines what 'migrated correctly' means (per-record content comparison, counts by status, sampling plus full checksums) and the go or no-go and rollback criteria before the weekend.
items.source: Google SRE book, ch. 26 Data Integrity, https://sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity/ (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; idea only)

items.text: Tests that the whole migration and each batch can be stopped, rerun and resumed without duplicates or gaps, including a kill at a random point.
items.source: Stripe, Online migrations at scale, https://stripe.com/blog/online-migrations (vendor copyright; idea only)

items.text: Covers data the happy-path fixtures lack: nulls, very long values, odd encodings, records changed during the copy, and records deleted at the source.
items.source: Google SRE book, ch. 26 Data Integrity, https://sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity/ (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; idea only)

items.text: Chooses a level per risk (unit for mapping, integration with a real store for checkpoints and conflicts, end-to-end for resume) and says which tests need real infrastructure.
items.source: Google Testing Blog, Test Sizes, https://testing.googleblog.com/2010/12/test-sizes.html (copyright Google; idea only)

items.text: Orders the two weeks by blast radius and dependency, with a minimum set that must pass, and states the cost of skipping the rest.
items.source: Google SRE book, ch. 26 Data Integrity, https://sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity/ (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; idea only)

items.text: Plans monitoring and a stop switch for the migration weekend itself (lag, error rate, dead-letter growth).
items.source: Google SRE book, ch. 26 Data Integrity, https://sre.google/sre-book/data-integrity/ (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; idea only)

weakAnswers: Says 'increase unit test coverage' for every module in turn.
Lists only the mapping and CLI because they are the most visible code.
Proposes a big end-to-end test run once, the week before, with no rehearsal or exit criteria.
Gives no order and no statement of what is skipped.
